body.heading: Retiring 'how was your day'
paragraphs: It is the most asked and least answered question in family life. The Question Game replaces it: one person brings one real question to dinner, everyone answers, and nobody is allowed to say 'fine.'
Good questions are specific and safe: What made you laugh today? What is something you are looking forward to? If our family had a mascot, what would it be, and why?

body.heading: Rules that keep it fun
paragraphs: Rotate who asks — kids' questions are reliably the best ones. Answers can be short; follow-up questions are the real game. And what gets said at the table stays gentle: mocking someone's answer ends the game faster than anything.
Within a few weeks, most families notice the shift: dinner becomes the place where the day gets properly shared, instead of the place where everyone reports 'fine' and reaches for a screen.

description: One question per dinner can turn 'how was your day' into the best conversation your family has all week.
